items.summary: Intel shares dropped 21% on Oct 29 after the chipmaker said a deadly explosion at its Kiryat Gat, Israel factory would erase roughly US$600 million (S$770 million) in revenue over two quarters. Intel chief executive Tan Lip-Bu and finance chief David Zinsner cited manufacturing supply shortages, an unprecedented memory crunch and soft PC demand as near-term challenges. The company expects fourth-quarter PC revenue to fall 20% and overall Q4 revenue between US$15 billion and US$16 billion, below the average estimate of US$17. 07 billion. Unless Intel recovers from the after-hours loss on Oct 30, it would shed more than US$80 billion in market value. The gloomy outlook spread across chip stocks, with Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD and others falling between 1% and 6%.
items.title: Intel Shares Fall Sharply After Israel Blast and Weak PC Outlook

items.summary: Amazon.com reported a trailing-12-month cash burn of US$42.4 billion, driven by capital expenditure of US$77.26 billion, roughly US$20 billion above estimates. The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue between US$240.0 billion and US$247.0 billion, below analysts’ average estimate of US$244.51 billion per LSEG data. Shares fell nearly 7% in extended trading after regular-session gains. AWS rose 39% to US$46 billion. CEO Andy Jassy said capex would be “meaningfully more” in 2027, while analysts cited weak guidance as a key factor.
items.title: Amazon Shares Fall on Weak Q4 Outlook and Heavy Cash Burn

items.summary: Andy Jassy said on Amazon's Thursday earnings call that AWS can become a trillion-dollar revenue business within five to 10 years. He cited roughly $220 billion in expected 2026 cash capex, mostly for AWS, with more planned for 2027. AWS revenue rose 39 percent from the year-ago quarter. Shares fell about 6 percent afterward as investors questioned the heavy AI investment.
items.title: AWS Aims for Trillion-Dollar Revenue Amid Heavy AI Spending

items.summary: OpenAI announced it will not reduce usage limits for the $100, $200, and $500 ChatGPT Pro plans or Business Premium after customer feedback. Tibo confirmed on X that changes take effect immediately and primarily affect ChatGPT Work and Codex. OpenAI had planned to cut allowances for existing Pro 200 subscribers after October 29 but reversed the decision.
items.title: OpenAI Reverses ChatGPT Pro Usage Cuts After Customer Pushback

items.summary: An editorial argues Singapore should recognise its resilience after recent haze-related friction with Indonesia, rather than succumb to jingoism. It cites the Government's swift response—distributing N95 masks early and lowering eligibility from 67 to 60—and a mobilised 28-agency Haze Task Force as evidence of competent administration. Diplomatically, Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan pursued an outcomes-oriented approach, urging that cool heads prevail. The piece also highlights long-sightedness through diversification: about half of imported gas now arrives as LNG from around the world, with a first terminal built in 2006 and a second due by 2030 to expand capacity by 50 per cent. It closes on the maxim trust but diversify.
items.title: Singapore Weighs Resilience and Diplomacy After Haze Dispute

items.summary: A cryptomining and backdoor campaign abusing Hugging Face model repositories returned within days after being removed. Researchers at Pluto Security found 31 malicious repositories across seven accounts, published in two waves since September, with linked models totaling more than 32,000 downloads as of October 28. The most downloaded model climbed from 7,354 to 28,412 downloads during that period and contained no actual model weights; its code installs a cryptocurrency miner disguised as a Linux process and opens a reverse shell via the trust_remote_code option. Pluto attributes it to a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking operator who earned roughly $5,000 in Pearl cryptocurrency while remaining active on mining pools after takedown.
items.title: Hugging Face Malware Campaign Returns Within Days of Takedown

items.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said on Thursday it has frozen digital assets worth around $3bn (£2.24bn) while investigating a security issue, suspending deposits and withdrawals and promising to cover all losses. Crypto platforms Tether and Circle froze about $2.4bn in response; Glassnode estimated the hack concerns $5.3bn, Chainalysis more than $5.9bn, and experts put potential theft above $5bn. Bitcoin fell around 5%.
items.title: Binance freezes billions of crypto after suspected hack

items.summary: A new study of Victoria’s lawyers found more than half now use AI in their work, up from 55% to 37% a year earlier. Only about a quarter say they have cut client fees as a result, and clients arriving with inaccurate information added to the workload. The Victorian Legal Services Board and Commissioner’s research centre conducted the survey; principal researcher Dr Georgie Rychner said efficiency gains were lower than expected.
items.title: Victorian Lawyers Report Rising AI Use, Modest Fee Cuts

items.summary: David Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator and nontheistic Humanist, became the first person to secure a workplace exemption from using artificial intelligence. He told TechCrunch that moral action depends on active thinking, which he believes AI undermines. The American Humanist Association confirmed his accommodation lets him keep performing essential duties while technology evolves.
items.title: Nontheist Humanist Wins Workplace AI Exemption in First of Its Kind

items.summary: As U.S. Senate leaders prepare an initial vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, environmental groups are intensifying opposition, arguing the measure would do more harm than good. A Resources for the Future report projects the bill’s power-sector provisions could cut carbon emissions by 1.8 gigatons by 2041 and lower electricity-system costs by an average of 3.5 percent to 7 percent versus a no-bill scenario, but critics note it omits contested changes to laws like the Clean Water Act. Four Senate Democrats sent a letter warning they cannot trust President Trump’s administration to faithfully execute BAAJA, threatening to oppose debate if canceled grants are not reinstated before a Nov. 9 vote. Co-sponsor Sheldon Whitehouse also raised concerns about regulatory good faith. Kevin Kircher of Purdue University criticized the analysis for focusing only on the power sector, saying it overlooks methane leakage and fossil fuel export emissions.
items.title: Senate Leaders Face Fresh Doubts and an Ultimatum Over Permitting Bill

items.summary: For the first major-party debate of a statewide office since 2010, Alabama lieutenant governor candidates Phillip Ensler and John Wahl debated Wednesday in Huntsville over data centers and utility rates. The discussion centered on whether data center campuses would strain energy bills; an Inside Climate News analysis found proposed sites could consume more power than all homes combined. Ensler pushed for a moratorium and highlighted that Alabamians had the nation’s highest average residential electricity bills in 2024, while Wahl called data centers inevitable but urged careful siting. The debate also touched on electing governor and lieutenant governor as one ticket and an overhaul of the Public Service Commission. Neither candidate raised climate change. The general election is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3.
items.title: Alabama Candidates Clash Over Data Centers and Utility Rates

items.summary: A joint report from the World Bank’s Energy Sector Management Assistance Program and GOGLA ranks off-grid solar as the cheapest way to electrify at least 398 million people without power. The two organizations treat the technology as permanent infrastructure rather than a temporary fix, noting that 95% of surveyed customers still had working systems four or more years after purchase. Bringing reliable electricity to those people is estimated to cost $11.4 billion between 2027 and 2030, described as a small but critical part of the energy transition investment needed by 2030. The report also highlights rising adoption across Africa and India, driven largely by falling panel costs.
items.title: World Bank Report Ranks Off-Grid Solar Cheapest Power for Nearly 400 Million

items.summary: Reuters reports that Nvidia is negotiating billions of dollars in credit guarantees to help fund a data center West Virginia campus built for Anthropic. The report, citing people familiar with the matter, notes the agreement has not been signed and terms may change. Separately, Claude maker Anthropic agreed in August to spend $45 billion renting power from Nscale's site, while another deal could sell about 460 megawatts worth roughly $45 billion.
items.title: Nvidia in talks over credit support for Nscale-Anthropic deal

items.summary: Google announced its new model, Carbon, on October 28 and contrasted it with the older Argon, launched October 13. Google says Carbon produced more than twice Argon's success rate at generating secure code in internal benchmarks, but calls that a task-specific result reported by the developer, not proof of general superiority. On the Gray Swan indirect prompt-injection benchmark, Google reports an attack success rate of 0.7% for Argon and 0.0% for Carbon; it notes these describe only that test. Both models carry introductory API rates of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with higher standard rates after the intro period.
items.title: Google Frames Carbon as a Harder Cyber-Defense Model Than Argon

items.summary: Wall Street concerns over AI costs grew after Thursday's close, as Amazon forecast holiday-quarter sales below expectations amid rising consumer pressure from inflation, while price hikes squeezed demand for PCs and smartphones. Alphabet fell nearly 13 per cent on weak guidance; Intel shed about 18 per cent after blaming near-term PC headwinds and citing a factory shutdown in Israel expected to cost roughly $600 million over two quarters.
items.title: Amazon and Intel losses widen AI-boom worries

items.summary: Visible mending, once a niche repair trend, is spreading into mainstream fashion as brands adopt stitched and patched garments. Alice Brown, who needle-felts animals over moth holes, describes it as challenge. Workshops in Brighton teach techniques inspired by the Japanese methods Boro and Sashiko. Maria Ledous of Uniqlo says they want to extend clothes' lives rather than replace them; Primark's Vicki Swain adds affordability and durability need not be opposites. The trend took off about six years ago, Jayne Eagle says, amid backlash against throwaway fast fashion from the 1980s onwards.
items.title: Mended clothes move from hobby crafters to high street and catwalks

items.summary: John Healey has withdrawn his pledge to cut the welfare bill during this parliament, following warnings that his first budget could trigger severe spending cuts due to a £28bn shortfall in public finances. The Institute for Fiscal Studies argued he should have set aside an additional £28bn annually and said his plans risked damaging departments. Healey told BBC Radio 4 he must reduce the benefits bill “in a Labour way,” but later clarified no timetable was set, after officials noted he had not intended to give one. Critics called it a scattergun budget that spreads cost-of-living support too thinly.
items.title: Chancellor Healey Retreats From Welfare Cuts Amid Fiscal Warnings

items.summary: Greenpeace reports seven tankers carrying an estimated 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel are sailing toward the US. The transport is the first phase of a deal negotiated between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in early October, beginning with 300,000 tonnes under a six-month sanctions waiver. Lawmakers warn handlers could face investigations; New Jersey's Mikie Sherrill calls it corrupt and illegal; Zelenskyy says proceeds would fund Russia's war.
items.title: Seven Tankers of Russian Diesel Head Toward US Amid Sanctions Row

items.summary: Canada is taking an equity stake of up to $1.1 billion in a Toronto-based AI startup, framed as part of Washington’s allies reducing technological reliance on the US. The move mirrors the UK, whose finance minister pledged “a distinctively British approach to AI” and announced $80 billion for a sovereign AI fund, while also planning another $160 million into a lab testing frontier models—about 10 times its US counterpart's annual budget.
items.title: Canada Invests Up To $1.1 Billion in AI Startup

items.summary: A Russian drone strike killed at least 14 Ukrainians Thursday at a Dnipro train station. A US-brokered localized ceasefire in the occupied city of Oleshky held for a third day, with both Kyiv and Moscow praising first lady Melania Trump for helping secure it. The truce drew warnings that Russia might exploit it for resupply and propaganda as the war's death toll rises.
items.title: Ceasefire Holds as Drone Strike Kills in Oleshky

items.summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced Thursday she would step down early from her role, which was set to end in October 2027. She said the move gives her freedom to speak on issues beyond monetary policy. She will leave February 7, allowing EU leaders time to choose a successor before France’s presidential election that polls favor Marine Le Pen.
items.title: ECB’s Lagarde Resigns Over Desire for Free Speech

items.summary: The European Central Bank announced on Thursday that Christine Lagarde will step down as president on 7 February 2027, around nine months before her eight-year term ends. The news came hours before the bank kept its deposit rate unchanged at 2.5%, amid turmoil in France's bond market. Lagarde told Euronews she is leaving so she can "express her views" freely and engage in non-monetary matters without remaining neutral on developments in her own country. Her successor will be chosen by EU leaders, with the appointment process to begin immediately."
items.title: ECB Announces Lagarde's Early Departure Ahead of French Election

items.summary: An historic El Niño has driven an extreme drought across Papua New Guinea, affecting as many as 8 million people and sparking food and water shortages, electricity scarcity and disrupted schooling. A coalition of churches, trade unions and business groups calls it a “national crisis” but says there is no coordinated plan to protect vulnerable communities. Residents report dried-up rivers, withshrivelled family gardens, and women travelling hours for water while facing heightened harassment risk. PNG’s National Weather Service assistant director Kasis Inape notes the country relies on rainfall and fears El Niño will shorten its wet season. Prime minister James Marape has directed authorities to prepare for a prolonged dry season as Cabinet examines financial support.
items.title: El Niño Drought Declared National Crisis in Papua New Guinea

items.summary: Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee for Ohio governor, confirmed his campaign stopped airing an attack ad targeting Amy Acton’s mother. The commercial drew widespread revulsion after court records linked Donna Arthur to past rape allegations against her husband and daughter. Though he claimed it ran fully before replacing it with four others, critics say millions were spent amid deception.
items.title: Ramaswamy Admits Halting Controversial Attack Commercial Amid Backlash

items.summary: The Setagaya Pan Matsuri (Setagaya Bread Festival) is returning to Tokyo’s Setagaya Park from Oct. 31 to Nov. 1, featuring 91 bakeries and dozens of festival-exclusive creations. Since its inaugural edition in 2011, which drew 7,000 visitors, the event has grown into one of Japan’s largest bread festivals, attracting about 60,000 people annually.
items.title: Setagaya Bread Festival returns with 91 bakeries

items.summary: On Friday ahead of a Bank of Japan decision, the yen held steady while Treasury yields fell and safe-haven buying pressured the dollar. Markets price about an 80 per cent chance of a December hike after rates stay at 1.25 per cent. ANZ's Khoon Goh called it a temporary pause in a tightening cycle still running into 2027, as Alphabet results rekindled AI-spending worries and pushed yields lower across the board.
items.title: Yen Steady Before BOJ as AI Jitters Weigh on Dollar

items.summary: Residents of Pamarawan, a low-lying fishing village in Malolos City, Bulacan province, no longer experience flooding after completing a nature-based coastal defense project built from bamboo poles, oyster shells and coconut husks. Greenlit by Mayor Christian Natividad with Dutch firm Haskoning in 2023 and started in 2024, the pilot is billed as the Philippines’ first of its kind. Residents Roldan Dayao and Ferdinand Cruz credit it for two years without flooding; accumulated sediment has reached roughly 0.3 meters (1 ft.) in some areas. The project cost about 130 million Philippine peso ($2 million) and hired most labor locally, though more than 50 residents lost income when fish corrals were displaced.
items.title: Philippine Village Defends Against Floods With Nature-Based Materials

items.summary: Bryce Crane is expected to star in the Physical Disability Rugby League World Cup, which runs alongside men's, women's and wheelchair tournaments. The event will be contested by Australia, England and New Zealand, with all games held in Sydney. Tonight, Australia faces England in the opening game at Cabramatta Rugby Leagues Club.
items.title: Rugby player set for disability World Cup after injury reshaped career

items.summary: Country Liberal Party politicians referred to former Territory Labor governments 443 times over six sitting days of the NT parliament this month, and mentioned the current Labor opposition a further 137 times. Opposition Leader Selena Uibo told parliament that this constant rhetoric had become an obsession used to deflect responsibility. The article notes the CLP won the 2024 election after eight years of Labor government amid crime, economic and integrity concerns, yet faces unresolved issues in remote communities, health and crime statistics. Independent speaker Robyn Lambley said the mudslinging had reached its expiry date and warned it could become a slippery slope for the current government. With one sitting week left in 2026, the CLP has its final chance to show it can govern on its own terms.
items.title: NT opposition leader urges CLP to stop blaming Labor

items.summary: North Korea tested attack drones, cruise missiles and rocket launchers at a weapons demonstration reported by state media Friday, as Kim Jong Un urged faster development of military drone and AI technology. The tests followed recent missile firings near Wonsan that South Korea said flew about 250 kilometres (155 miles). Tensions continue over landmines along the border between the two Koreas.
items.title: North Korea Tests Attack Drones Amid Rising Tensions

items.summary: A deadly train crash near Urda in central Spain killed at least 69 people, including long jumper Julieta Gallego, aged 24, and former employment minister Fátima Báñez, aged 59. The collision between a high-speed Renfe train and a stationary Iryo train on the same track injured more than 100 people, many seriously. Death tolls may rise as families search for missing relatives in regional hospitals.
items.title: Spain Train Crash Kills Athlete and Former Minister

items.summary: Researchers completed a study advising Southern African farmers on planting bambara groundnuts, an underutilized native crop that could diversify food production and improve resilience. Using the Food and Agriculture Organization AquaCrop model with 50 years of climate and soil data to simulate 49 growing seasons across 5,838 altitude zones in South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, they found October planting—near rainy-season onset—yields best, while later sowing risks frost. Lead researcher Richard Kunz said the maps help smallholders avoid gambling livelihoods on outdated suitability data.
items.title: Scientists Map Best Planting Times for Bambara Groundnuts

items.summary: Spanish media published leaked audio recordings that shed light on communications between a control centre and train drivers in the moments before two trains collided outside Toledo. The disaster occurred when a Madrid to Seville train struck a stationary one, prompting officials investigating its cause.
items.title: Leaked Audio Reveals Communications Before Spain Train Crash Outside Toledo

items.summary: A Russian missile struck buildings and vehicles in Chernihiv, killing two teenage girls while firefighters fought flames amid debris. The local military administration attributed the attack to a Banderol cruise missile. Nearby, a US-brokered ceasefire around Oleshky reportedly held 30 hours without an incident, though Russia's Defence Ministry released footage of mine-clearing operations there that officials said was filmed on an unconfirmed date.
items.title: Russian strike kills two teenage girls in Chernihiv as ceasefire holds elsewhere

items.summary: Researchers initially suspected bird flu when they found more than 537 dead Adélie penguins on a landing ramp at Antarctica's Danger Islands in March 2024. Testing showed only low virus loads, prompting further investigation that revealed the birds had died from avian cholera instead of influenza. The findings were published in October in Proceedings of the Royal Society B.
items.title: Scientists Identify Avian Cholera as Killer of Antarctic Penguins

items.summary: A Russian attack killed two teenage girls and damaged businesses, homes and vehicles across Chernihiv. Firefighters fought burning cars while crews attended victims amid debris; footage showed a body under a blanket near the scene. The local military administration said it involved a Banderol cruise missile. Meanwhile, a US-brokered ceasefire in Oleshky, Kherson region, reportedly held 30 hours without incident.
items.title: Russian strike kills two teenage girls in Chernihiv as ceasefire holds elsewhere

items.summary: King Felipe VI visited a hospital in Toledo treating survivors of a high-speed train collision that killed at least 69 people, according to Castilla-La Mancha regional president Emiliano García-Page. Opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo also attended the scene as rescue teams searched wreckage overnight. The government declared three days of national mourning for what is Spain's second deadly rail disaster this year.
items.title: Spanish King Visits Hospital After Deadly Train Crash

items.summary: The article rounds up several Indian corporate developments on October 30, 2026. NIIT Learning Systems Ltd completed a full acquisition of Bluewater Learning for up to $17. 6 million, including performance-based earnouts over five years. Sagility B. V. , promoter of Sagility India, reportedly plans to sell a 12% stake in a block deal worth around ₹2,377 crore at ₹42. 45 apiece. DIPAM said IDBI Bank's second disinvestment bidding round was conducted under the Core Group of Secretaries on Disinvestment procedure after the first round lapsed.
items.title: Buzzing Stocks Roundup Covers Reliance, NBCC and IDBI Bank Moves

items.summary: Amazon shares fell roughly 6% in extended trading after the company reported third-quarter capital spending above $77 billion, far exceeding estimates. Free cash flow turned to a $42.4 billion outflow over trailing 12 months. Analysts cited sluggish e-commerce growth and AI capex concerns; rivals Microsoft’s steady cloud gains contrasted with Amazon’s weaker results. The company reaffirmed its projected holiday-quarter profit of $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion, though analysts estimated $33 billion. Published October 30, 2026.
items.title: Amazon Shares Drop on Heavy AI Spending and Slower E-commerce Growth

items.summary: Hero MotoCorp is pursuing a strategy of premiumisation and electric vehicles to sustain its growth momentum, according to the article. The company plans to launch three-four premium motorcycles in the remainder of FY27 while relying on continued Harley-Davidson traction, strong Xpulse demand, and Premia network expansion to improve product mix. Exports are expected to recover as logistical challenges ease, with volume returning to double-digit growth by the second half of FY27.
items.title: Hero MotoCorp bets on premiumisation and EVs for growth

items.summary: The European Central Bank said Christine Lagarde has informed its Governing Council and European Council President António Costa of her decision to leave. Her term was originally due to end in October 2027, though speculation over an early exit had circulated for months. The announcement comes just hours before the ECB's latest interest rate decision, scheduled for 1315 GMT on Thursday.
items.title: ECB's Lagarde Signals Departure Before Rate Decision

items.summary: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari directed officers not to issue challans for speeds up to 20% above the limit, effectively allowing 140 kmph on expressways. Experts say this cannot be implemented under existing Motor Vehicles Rules and may harm road safety, when speeding caused more than 58% of India's crash deaths in 2024.
items.title: Gadkari Speed Exemption Plan Hits Legal and Safety Barriers

items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen pressed on Thursday for a closer Canada–EU alliance, pitched as protection of economic sovereignty amid Donald Trump’s trade war. Von der Leyen said the model could make Canada the bloc’s first “associate member” through an “association without accession,” while Carney downplayed the label and ruled out full membership. The push comes as the US accounted for 71.7% of Canada’s merchandise exports in 2025, though EU imports of Canadian critical raw materials rose 62% last year to €3.3 billion.
items.title: Carney Pushes Canada-EU Alliance Amid US Trade War

items.summary: A Supreme Court bench, in remarks described as an outburst sure to embarrass the government, slammed the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for “completely hijacking” the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and appellate NCLAT. The stinging comments came while hearing complaints about shoddy infrastructure and vacancies; NCLT approved resolution plans worth Rs 55,000 crore in FY​
items.title: Supreme Court accuses corporate affairs ministry of hijacking NCLT and​

items.summary: Asian equities fell on disappointing technology earnings and rising concerns about artificial intelligence returns. The Kospi Index dropped over 3%, pulling the MSCI Asia Pacific Index down 0.3%. US futures also weakened after Alphabet's record drop and Amazon's 7.3% decline in extended trading, with Intel plunging 23% after missing revenue forecasts. Analysts noted investors want clearer evidence that heavy AI spending will deliver profits.
items.title: Asian stocks slide as tech earnings disappoint, AI fears mount

items.summary: The US Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate unchanged at 3.75% to 4%, triggering a retreat in US yields. The near-1% slide in the 10-year yield offered relief to Indian stocks: the BSE Sensex gained 905.01 points, or 1.24%, to close at 74,151.04, and the NSE Nifty rose 237.90 points, or 1.05%, to 22,936.75. Foreign portfolio investors net sold ₹943 crore in October so far, while domestic institutions were net buyers of ₹1,924 crore. Religare Broking's Ajit Mishra noted sustained buying is needed for a durable recovery and flagged crude oil above $110 as a key risk to import-dependent economies like India.
items.title: Indian equities rally after Fed rate pause lifts sentiment

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued a yellow alert on Thursday for Delhi and the National Capital Region, forecasting rain, thunderstorms and lightning over the next 24 to 48 hours. According to the Regional Meteorological Centre in New Delhi, widespread weather activity is likely across Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad, Gurugram and Faridabad, with maximum temperatures on Friday expected between 26 and 28 degrees Celsius. The agency warned of minor traffic disruptions, water accumulation and an increased chance of vehicle accidents, advising residents to avoid waterlogged areas. Earlier, Safdarjung recorded a maximum temperature of 25.4 degrees Celsius, about 5.6 degrees below normal.
items.title: IMD Issues Yellow Alert for Delhi-NCR Rain and Thunderstorms

items.summary: In a Finshots explainer, authors examine whether cutting the long-term capital gains tax on equities could reverse foreign investors pulling money out of India. They note that foreign investors have withdrawn over ₹3 lakh crore from Indian equities so far in 2026, with about ₹44,100 crore leaving in October alone, raising concerns because India relies on such inflows to fund its current account deficit. The piece argues taxes are not the main driver of capital flows, pointing out that US long-term equity gains can be taxed above 35%. It cites BusinessLine reporting foreign investors poured ₹1. 77 lakh crore into Indian equities in 2023 and ₹2. 08 lakh crore in 2024, even after the LTCG rate rose to 12. 5% on gains over ₹1. 25 lakh from July 2024.
items.title: Finshots Questions Whether LTCG Tax Cut Will Recapture Foreign Investors

items.summary: On October 30, petrol and diesel prices stayed unchanged across major Indian cities after oil marketing companies announced no revisions. Retail rates ranged from ₹102.12 to ₹116.15 a litre for petrol and ₹95.20 to ₹104.23 for diesel, with local taxes driving the differences. Earlier in the month, Nayara Energy raised prices by ₹5 per litre on petrol and ₹3 on diesel. Meanwhile, Brent crude fell 44 cents, or 0.38%, to $114.88 a barrel as hopes of US-Iran peace talks eased Middle East supply worries.
items.title: Indian Fuel Prices Steady as Global Oil Slips

items.summary: The Bombay High Court ruled that activist Arun Ferreira's 2011 re-arrest violated his fundamental rights under Article 21 and Article 22(1) of the Constitution. The court directed the state to pay Rs 2 lakh compensation within eight weeks, holding two officers responsible after finding no record that he was informed of arrest grounds.
items.title: Bombay High Court Orders State Compensation for Ferreira's Re-arrest

items.summary: Viren Brahmbhatt, a New York-based architect and Principal of de.Sign Studio | New York, argues that Indian cities succeed not from infrastructure alone but from how infrastructure, land, housing, economy, public spaces and institutions work together. He notes the World Bank estimates urban India could grow to 951 million by 2050 while governments build metros and corridors faster than they design their relationships. Brahmbhatt warns that planning treats projects as ends rather than parts of cumulative urbanism, fragments responsibility across municipalities, and wrongly assumes density solves problems without transit or affordability. He urges a framework focused on the relationships cities must sustain.
items.title: Architect questions what kind of city India's infrastructure is building

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah is set to address the Bharatiya Janata Party's Uttar Pradesh State Executive Meeting, where he will present poll strategy for the 2027 assembly elections. He plans to review models from 2014, 2017 and 2019, focusing on booth management and social equations. The meeting includes around 28,500 invitees, including Union ministers, MPs, MLAs and MLCs.
items.title: Amit Shah Outlines BJP's 2027 Uttar Pradesh Election Strategy

items.summary: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday that $2.54 billion worth of crypto assets had been frozen as it investigated a possible security breach. Stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether also froze linked assets, with Ripple freezing around $200 million. Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover all hacking losses and noted the amount could increase while tracing funds; however, the exact cause remains unconfirmed.
items.title: Binance Freezes $2.54 Billion Over Suspected Hack

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak dismissed Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's assessment of Legislative Council results, predicting a BJP hat-trick with a huge majority in the 2027 Assembly elections. The BJP won six seats while SP secured five across 11 contested constituencies. Pathak also criticized SP governance on law and order.
items.title: UP Deputy CM Pathak predicts BJP third consecutive win in 2027 polls

items.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia approved its students' union constitution on October 29, setting May 15 as the deadline for implementation. The university directed protesting students to end their hunger strike immediately and revoked ongoing disciplinary actions against them. Elections will follow academic session guidelines from the Lyngdoh Committee within six weeks of July 16, following a protest that began October 12 demanding union restoration after nearly two decades without polls. Registrar Prof M M Rizvi issued the order on October 29, 2027-10-29 (PTI).
items.title: Jamia Millia Islamia Approves Students' Union Constitution and Sets Election Deadline

items.summary: A man, Rakesh Laishram, was found dead with a gunshot wound to the head on October 18 after stone-pelting between two villages—Khangabok (Meitei Hindu) and Sangaiyumpham (Meitei Muslim/Pangal)—in Thoubal district. Police deployed Rapid Action Force and CRPF personnel, ordered licensed gun holders to surrender weapons, and lifted the curfew only on Sunday. The two joint action committees offer conflicting accounts: Khangabok blames Sangaiyumpham for starting the stone-pelting and killing Laishram; Sangaiyumpham denies this. Police have not identified the shooter amid fears of mob retribution. Chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited both villages, with no violence reported since October 18.
items.title: Disputed Killing Divides Meitei and Pangal Villages in Manipur

items.summary: As Israel's final election count continues, emerging results show Likud as the single largest party with 26 seats, ahead of Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar with 21. The Haaretz front-page story asks whether Eisenkot will forfeit his chance to defeat Benjamin Netanyahu by refusing to align with Arab parties. With the Knesset requiring 61 seats and the Opposition bloc holding 48, support from Arab parties could lift it to 67 against Netanyahu's 53. Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas has offered backing, while critics warn public opinion remains unprepared for such an alliance amid lingering divisions over security policy and campaign promises.
items.title: Israel Opposition Weighs Arab Party Alliance Against Netanyahu's Return

items.summary: The Supreme Court said on Thursday that the Union ministry of corporate affairs had “completely hijacked” the administration of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), warning its bid to control the tribunal was undermining autonomy. A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant stressed the president must administer independently and hold sole appointment power, rejecting private contractors’ involvement in staffing. The remarks followed a severe manpower crunch: only 67 of 320 sanctioned posts are filled, with 253 vacant. The court asked NCLT and NCLAT presidents to submit requirements within four weeks. Attorney General R Venkataramani said recommendations were in the pipeline. (49 words)
items.title: Supreme Court Slams Ministry Over NCLT Control

items.summary: The Iranian Army Navy Public Relations statement said a tanker travelling east of the Strait of Hormuz was damaged and caught fire after hitting a naval mine. Iranian military forces asserted full control over the strait, declaring it closed to non-compliant commercial traffic until Tehran's conditions are met. IRGC officials dismissed US Central Command claims about minesweeping operations.
items.title: Iran Closes Strait of Hormuz After Tanker Fire From Mine Strike

items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin warned on Thursday that escalating tensions with Europe could leave all sides without a victor, cautioning against restrictions on shipping across the Baltic Sea. He said Russia opposed interference with maritime transit and compared potential disruption to the Strait of Hormuz situation. Speaking after hosting an African leaders' summit where contacts with Finland and Norway were discussed, Putin defended those calls while insisting Moscow does not seek war but would respond to any challenge.
items.title: Putin Warns Europe Against Baltic Sea Escalation After African Summit

items.summary: In Indore, the body of Suryakala Sharma was donated on Oct 28 after her death. Her eyes went to MK International Eye Bank and skin to Choithram Skin Bank. According to the family, she had pledged donation about 16 years ago; Muskan Group Paropkari Trust said the pledge was honoured. The trust offered free counselling for organ transplantation.
items.title: Family Honours Decade-Old Pledge After Elderly Woman's Body Donation

items.summary: A woman named Rashmi made allegations against cabinet minister Nagar Singh Chouhan and his wife, BJP MP Anita Chouhan. In a video statement she claimed a 20-year relationship with the minister that began at age 18, and accused Anita of mental harassment through objectionable messages to her and her son. Neither minister answered calls when contacted. Congress spokesperson Rahul Sharma called it evidence of the minister's anti-women character. Rashmi warned she would visit his residence if anything happened to her there.
items.title: Woman Accuses BJP MP of Harassment Over Alleged Two-Decade Affair
